touches.text: Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. Akien: "being put in service only requires that it's the best we can do now. only requires 80% trust."

Hourly: an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9) reseals every yellow component and everything that depends on it. Commit a is fine and commit b is fine, and an hour later the run finds a new red. That is the system doing what it was designed to do (Akien 2026-11-13), and the window to search is one hour's landings. Hourly confirmed by Akien 2026-11-13: "perfect. yes that."
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machine build_inspector; db client.

Deleting code is about running code, not about the record of what happened. A retired path that something still CALLS is the defect; a retired path named by a record of what passed through (history, state, validations, verdicts, a measured fixture) is not. Requirements that police history are de-emphasized, because the aim is less history noise in front of Claude, not hidden history (Law 5). Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#99 (ticket c8e421aac06e's measured fixture names skills/ruled/intention+why.json and the retirement tooth read it as a caller): "we are trying to remove as much of the history as we can. not hiding it, but reducing the noise you're exposed to. time to de-emphasize requirements like that."
validation_store: reads and writes seals. USERS: the tester.

Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.

Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
Device: its own process, in the rack, on the bus (2).
A device owns its state: only the device writes under its own ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.
